LEGAL CAREER ADVICE PODCAST WITH HARRISON BARNES

25 Reasons to Move to a New Firm

In this comprehensive episode, Harrison Barnes outlines 25 compelling reasons attorneys choose to move to new law firms—and why those moves often lead to greater success and fulfillment. From career growth to cultural misalignment, Harrison breaks down the real motivations behind lateral moves and offers guidance on when change is the right choice.

Podcast Highlights:

  • The most common—and overlooked—reasons attorneys seek new opportunities
  • How firm culture, lack of mentorship, or stalled advancement can signal it’s time to move
  • Strategic moves that can boost compensation, work-life balance, and long-term potential
  • Why staying too long in the wrong environment can harm your career
  • How to evaluate whether your current firm supports your goals

DAILY JOB SEARCH ADVICE

Eliot Spitzer’s Lessons: Finding Strength in Your Dark Side

Harrison Barnes | 08-18-2025

When you try to mask or suppress aspects of your personality, those traits will inevitably come to the fore anyway. You need to develop a comprehensive understanding of yourself, including your darker or deeply buried traits; once you know how your dark side limits and controls you, the better you will do in your life and career. Self-discovery will ultimately lead to inner peace, which in turn will enable you to more fully develop your goals.

Fastest-Growing Legal Practice Areas 2026: Where Firms Are Hiring

Attorneys who want to stay ahead of the legal job market in 2026 cannot afford to guess which practice areas are growing. Law Firm Partner Compensation: Equity vs Non-Equity and ROI Explained

Law firm partnership has never been a simple “make partner and share profits” milestone. Today’s partnership landscape is increasingly tiered, metric-driven, and designed to manage firm profitability—often by expanding non-equity roles while concentrating equity ownership. This recent report, “Law Firm Partner Compensation Structures: Analysis of Equity vs Non-Equity Economics and ROI,” lays out what has changed, why it matters, and how attorneys and firm leaders can evaluate partnership opportunities using an ROI lens.

Read the full report here: Law Firm Partner Compensation Structures: Analysis of Equity vs Non-Equity Economics and ROI
